setup.Xi_condition: tau(i t)=widehat(Phi)(t)=0, in the declared Fourier-Laplace convention

fourier_solution.regularity: at a Xi zero the numerator vanishes at xi=t, removing the apparent pole to the order supplied by the zero multiplicity
fourier_solution.qualification: normalization constants depend on the Fourier convention and do not affect vanishing

adjoint_residual.interpretation: a Hilbert-transform boundary value of the nonnegative spectral density |widehat(Phi)|^2
adjoint_residual.Green_identity: its real part vanishes automatically on the seam, but its imaginary part is the displayed principal-value integral

promotion_criterion.unchanged_history_enters_minimal_paired_: requires both widehat(Phi)(t)=0 and H(|widehat(Phi)|^2)(t)=0, plus the arithmetic adjoint rows
promotion_criterion.strength: strictly stronger than the Xi seam-zero condition unless a new source identity relates the value and conjugate boundary data

finite_test.nonzero_result: falsifies unchanged-state promotion into the minimal adjoint-complete Green pencil
finite_test.zero_result: is evidence for an additional conjugate-boundary identity but does not establish all ordinates or completion

architectural_consequence: The source-derived Rosenbrock Xi pencil remains valid, but its natural kernel state generally cannot be reused unchanged as the kernel of the minimal conservative paired pencil. A viable conservative realization must add a source-derived arithmetic coordinate that cancels this Hilbert-transform residual while preserving the seam mismatch divisor, or use a different positive boundary law.
conclusion: On the seam, the missing lower Green equation is not another copy of Xi=0. It is an independent Hilbert-transform condition. This makes the exact obstruction computationally testable and prevents endpoint mismatch from being mistaken for adjoint promotion.
